title: Compatible adjunction-unit markings identify canonical quotient diagrams
statement: For a commutative ring A, ideal I, and specified left adjoints L_n to exact derived restriction D(A/I^(n+1)) to D(A) [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], define the canonical consecutive quotient map by transposing the preceding level unit. Let K_n have consecutive quotient-linear maps v_n, and let e_n:L_n(C)≅K_n. If these maps satisfy the displayed unit-transition equations, then e_n after scalar restriction define an isomorphism of the entire inverse diagrams. Neither finiteness, projectivity, normalization nor completeness is required.

source.place: Tag 09C6, compatibility of the finite-projective quotient diagram; More on Algebra, Tag 09AW, actual reduction units.

proof.text: Define the canonical quotient transition as the inverse adjunction Hom map of the preceding unit followed by the iterated scalar-restriction isomorphism. The Hom equivalence immediately proves its unit equation.

Transpose the proposed consecutive marking square. Cancel the invertible scalar-restriction comparison and use its naturality. The assumed unit-transition equation then proves equality of transposes, and injectivity gives the square.

Use the squares to form a natural transformation of sequential diagrams. Every component is the image of an isomorphism under scalar restriction, hence invertible. The natural transformation is therefore an isomorphism.

For two choices of quotient left adjoints, the unique isomorphism of left adjoints carries the specified units to each other. The transpose equation gives compatible markings, so the proved diagram-marking theorem identifies the entire canonical diagrams. This proves the choice-independence step used by the canonical representative comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem finitePerfectAdicQuotientDiagram_marking
    {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (L : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))))
    (adj : ∀ n : ℕ, L n ⊣ DerivedCategory.adicLevelRestriction I n)
    (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t} A))
    (K : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))))
    (v : ∀ n : ℕ, K (n + 1) ⟶ (DerivedCategory.adicStepRestriction I n).obj (K n))
    (e : ∀ n : ℕ, (L n).obj C ≅ K n)
    (he : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (adj (n + 1)).unit.app C ≫
          (DerivedCategory.adicLevelRestriction I (n + 1)).map (e (n + 1)).hom ≫
          DerivedCategory.adicTowerTransition I K v n =
        (adj n).unit.app C ≫
          (DerivedCategory.adicLevelRestriction I n).map (e n).hom) :
    Nonempty (finitePerfectAdicQuotientDiagram I L adj C ≅
      Functor.ofOpSequence (X := fun n ↦
        (DerivedCategory.adicLevelRestriction I n).obj (K n))
        (DerivedCategory.adicTowerTransition I K v))
